children.text: Website development for a psychologist is not just a business card with contact details — it's a full instrument that builds trust before a client ever reaches out. Unlike typical business niches, where a visitor compares prices and specifications, someone looking for a psychologist or therapist primarily evaluates safety and professionalism. That's why a website for a private practice needs a different approach: a clear presentation of your therapeutic method, your education and certifications, and careful handling of personal data.

I develop websites for psychologists and therapists with a focus on technical SEO, modern AI-search optimization (AEO and GEO), and a client-friendly structure. A site built this way is found not only through classic Google search but also through AI assistants like ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews — thanks to correct Schema.org structured markup and semantically organized content.

A website for a psychologist includes booking integration through channels convenient for the client, a blog answering common questions about therapy, and a responsive design that works equally well on phone and desktop. This approach helps a practitioner attract clients from search steadily, without constant ad spend, while building long-term reputation through a quality, trustworthy site.

Particular attention in developing a website for a psychologist goes to loading speed and Core Web Vitals — a slow site loses visitors before they even read about your approach. Interface accessibility for people with different information-processing needs also matters. Every element of the site, from heading structure to button copy, is designed to guide the visitor toward booking a consultation, not just to look attractive.

children.text: The cost depends on scope. A focused one-page website with custom design, development, and SEO/AEO/GEO optimization starts from 2000 €. A multi-page site with a blog, trust-building sections about your approach and credentials, and booking integration starts from 3500 €. The final price depends on how many pages you need, the complexity of booking and messenger integrations, and whether a blog is included. To get an exact quote, describe your practice and I'll prepare a proposal tailored to your needs.

I build sites with correct Schema.org structured data, a semantic content architecture, and clear, factual presentation of your services and expertise — this is the technical foundation that helps AI systems accurately understand, cite, and recommend your practice, not just classic search engines. As AI-powered search grows, this kind of preparation increasingly determines whether potential clients find you at all. It's not a separate add-on service — it's built into the site from the start.

items.question: Can you optimize the site for AI tools like ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews?

children.text: Yes, confidentiality is treated as a core design requirement, not an afterthought. I avoid tracking tools and third-party integrations that could expose visitor or client data, and I'm careful with how any testimonials, case mentions, or personal details are handled — always with proper care and consent. For a psychology or therapy practice, this matters as much as the visual design: visitors need to feel safe on your site before they ever consider reaching out, and a website that mishandles privacy signals undermines that trust immediately.

items.question: Will client confidentiality be respected in the site's design?

children.text: Yes. I integrate booking systems like Calendly, direct messenger links (WhatsApp, Telegram), or a custom contact form — whatever fits how you actually work with clients. The goal is to remove friction: a visitor who has decided to reach out should be able to do it in one click, through the channel they're most comfortable with, rather than hunting for your contact details or filling out a complicated form. This directly affects how many visitors convert into booked sessions.

items.question: Can the site include booking through Calendly, WhatsApp, or similar tools?

children.text: Yes. I build multilingual sites with a correct SEO structure for each language and work with practitioners across Europe and internationally. This matters especially for online practices, where your client base isn't limited to one city or country — a properly built multilingual site lets you be found by clients searching in their own language, without diluting your visibility in any single market.
